chunks: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated from his father, from Ahmad ibn Hilal al-Abartai, from Ibn Abi Umair, from Saeed ibn Ghazwan, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said in his hadith: 'Surely Allah chose the prophets from among the people, and chose the messengers from among the prophets, and chose me from among the messengers, and chose Ali from among me, and chose Hasan and Husain from among Ali, and chose the successors from among Husain. The ninth of them is their Qaim, and he is their apparent and their concealed.'

key_terms.قَائِمَهُمْ: Their Qaim (The Riser/One who stands for justice)

ai.seo_question: Who is the ninth Imam and what is his title in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kitab al-Ghayba* establishes the theological hierarchy of divine election (*khiyarat*), tracing the lineage of authority from the Prophets to the Twelve Imams, with a specific emphasis on the progeny of Husain (AS). It identifies the ninth Imam as the *Qaim* (al-Mahdi), highlighting his dual role as the manifest and hidden reality of the Imamate, a concept central to Twelver eschatology and the doctrine of occultation. The narration underscores the continuity of spiritual and political leadership, affirming the Imams as the chosen successors who preserve the inner and outer truths of Islam.
